title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Deck and fence maintenance
audience: Deck and fence maintenance owners who want repeat seasonal work and referrals from homeowners, rental managers and body corporates they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Make a review or referral request after the client confirms the result, and make it easy to decline
Write a seasonal maintenance offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it
Write referral reward terms, including the payment condition, before any referral is made

instruction.heading: Ask after the client has checked the result
instruction.body: Ask for a review or referral after the client has walked the finished deck or fence, confirmed it is right, and paid. Ask in one sentence, name the next step you want, and make it easy to decline. Record the date and the answer. In one Baylor Keller Center experiment, a late reminder brought more reviews than an immediate one, which is one experiment, not a rule. A marketing association piece (AMA, January 2023) says that some services need more time before customers can judge them, so match the timing to the work. A deck may take a season to show its result.

instruction.heading: Keep review requests within the platform rules
instruction.body: A review link or QR code is allowed. Do not write reviews for clients, invent them, or ask only satisfied clients, which is called review gating. Google bans discounts or goods in return for reviews. The ACCC says any incentive must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says.

instruction.heading: Offer the seasonal visit in writing before the client leaves
instruction.body: Propose a dated next step at sign-off: an annual deck inspection and clean before the warm months, or a fence check after the wet season. Put the scope, the interval and the price approach in writing, and confirm the client agrees before the schedule changes. The research did not find evidence of repeat rates for these services, so treat the plan as a test. A vendor describes recurring service agreements and recommends a short follow-up after each job, but its figures are vendor claims. If a plan renews automatically, the renewal terms must be clear, and new unfair-trading rules are due to take effect on 1 July 2027, so check them before you offer auto-renewal.

instruction.heading: Check in and re-contact in the right season
instruction.body: A check-in about ninety days after the work is a choice to test, not a benchmark. Re-contact before a seasonal need, such as a pre-summer clean or a post-wet-season fence check, with a short, factual message and a clear way to opt out. Any message that promotes a service can be commercial even when it is framed as a reminder, so check it against the Spam Act before sending. Honour an opt-out within five working days.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward and write the payment condition, which is normally that the referred person has completed a paid job. Give the referrer a copy. A 2023 study in the Journal of Marketing Research found that stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals across seven studies. Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent. Check any cash-based reward with an adviser. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so those points are not settled here.

procedure: After each job is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the seasonal offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the client.
Schedule the check-in for the interval that suits the work, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred job is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A homeowner has her 20 square metre deck re-sealed and its loose rail fixed. She is pleased with the result and is offered a seasonal visit: an annual inspection and clean before the warm months, at a fixed price for the visit. The offer is written and the next date is given.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must the offer say, and what happens if she declines or the plan renews automatically?
workedExamples.reasoning: The offer states the scope (inspection, clean, minor fixings and a short report), the interval (annual, before the warm months), the price approach (a fixed price per visit set from the owner's own cost), and what is excluded, such as board renewal found necessary at inspection. If she declines, the owner records her answer and does not keep sending sales messages except as the Spam Act permits. If the plan renews automatically, the renewal date, the cancellation method and the total must be in writing. The unfair-trading rules due from 1 July 2027 are a reason to check the terms before any auto-renewal is offered.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Seasonal offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of seasonal re-contact dates for the service
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has seen the finished deck or fence.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, when the client has confirmed the result is right.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a client's photo of the deck or name without consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or using an auto-renewal with unclear terms.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list and honour it at once. Write renewal and cancellation terms in full before offering them.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, client details are personal information. Whether it applies is not settled in the research, so check the OAIC's small business guidance.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder. Every commercial message needs a working unsubscribe, honoured within five working days.

A referral does not extend the licence or authority of the business that accepts the work. Accept only work your licence and insurance cover in the state where it is done. Queensland and NSW thresholds differ, and the Victorian home-warranty threshold is unresolved. This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every seasonal offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer
Seasonal offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has checked the result, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the seasonal visit in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a client for a review or referral?
options: Before the boards are laid, so the client feels committed
After the client has checked the finished result and confirmed it is right
Only when the client has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to post a review with her name and a photo of her new deck. What do you need?
options: Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional
Her consent for the name and photo you plan to publish

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does this lesson say to propose the seasonal visit?
